replies.reply:
OPTIONS:
- Ask Ambrose what he knows about the clock and the sleeping children, and whether the clock's racing has anything to do with it (for: finding out what's wrong before I spend a button on anything)
- Ask Ambrose what he'd charge to put up a small shed in the nettle patch beside the tower (for: getting nearer to four walls and a door that locks, paid for fair)
- Go south across the square to Fizzlewick's and ask Nell what she knows, and what a waking tonic might cost (for: a way to help the children, if it's cheap enough)
* Ask Ambrose why the clock is ticking so loud and fast, and whether he's seen the sleepers' missing shadows (for: learning what's wrong before I spend a button)
DO: I look up at the chains twitching and say slow, "Ambrose. Clock's running fast. Loud, too. Three days the children sleep, and now this. Is it the toys? Tell me what you know. I'll not ask you for owt else." I keep my hand on my sock and wait for his answer.
JOURNAL: I can't sleep, and the clock sounds wrong the same way the town does, so Ambrose is the best place to start, and it costs me no buttons. I want my own walls someday, but not while the children lie asleep with no shadows and I know nothing about why.

OPTIONS:
- Ask Ambrose what he knows about the clock and the sleeping children, since the clock ticks wrong tonight (for: learning whether the clock and the toys are connected)
- Ask Ambrose his price for a small shed in the nettle patch beside the tower (for: working toward four walls and a door that locks)
- Walk across the square to Nell Fizzlewick's and ask whether she has a tonic that wakes sleepers (for: finding a way to help the children)
- Go up to the Gearloft and look at why the chains twitch and the clock runs fast (for: finding the cause myself without owing anyone)
* Ask Ambrose plainly what the clock is doing and whether it has to do with the toys (for: learning what is wrong before I spend any buttons)
DO: I look up at the twitching chains and then at Ambrose. "Clock's fast tonight. Fair's fair, you'd tell me if it was the toys." I wait slow, counting the ticks under my breath. "Is it? Three days the children sleep, and now this."
JOURNAL: I'd sooner know what's wrong before I spend any of my six buttons, and Ambrose is right here and costs nothing to ask. If the clock and the toys are bound together, I'll know where to put my back into it, and I'll save my buttons for the shed once the town is right again.

OPTIONS:
- Ask Ambrose what he knows about the clock and the sleeping children, and why it ticks so fast tonight (for: learning whether the clock and the peddler are connected)
- Go south to Fizzlewick's and ask Nell what she's heard about the toys, and what a waking tonic might cost (for: finding a way to wake the children without spending my buttons rashly)
- Ask Ambrose his price for a small shed in the nettle patch (for: working toward four walls and a door that locks)
* Speak to Ambrose about the fast ticking and the sleeping children (for: finding out what he knows before I spend anything)
DO: I look up at the chains twitching and say slow to Ambrose, "Clock's loud tonight. Faster than it ought. Ten days of coal I've carried past it and never heard it so. Children asleep three days, no shadows on them. You know aught of that, Ambrose? I'll pay for the telling, fair's fair, if it's not dear."
JOURNAL: Buttons are few, so I'd sooner learn something before I spend any. Ambrose has kept this clock fifty years, and the ticking and the sleeping children both started wrong at once. I'm still working toward my own door, but I can't sleep easy while the hearths stay cold where the children lie.

OPTIONS:
- Talk to Pip Pumbleton about her brother's missing shadow and what she's seen (for: learning what is really happening to the children, and showing I care)
- Go to Fizzlewick's and see what Nell might make for five buttons (for: a small fine thing of my own, and maybe gossip about the peddler)
- Ask Mags Ragwort what she's heard about Mister Tibbersnatch and whether she buys or sells anything unusual (for: a lead, and maybe a bit of trade)
* Walk over to Pip and ask her what she knows about the toys and the shadows (for: understanding the trouble, and not being alone in the dark square)
DO: I tuck my shawl round my shoulders and sweep over to Pip. "Goodness, Pip Pumbleton, you look like a cross little lamp-wick, standing there wide awake. Tell me about your brother's shadow, truly. What did you see the night he wound that toy? I've a thimble, a needle-quick wit and nothing better to do, and I'd like to help."
JOURNAL: Pip is the only one here who is actually doing something about the sleeping children, and I can't sleep anyway, so I'd rather be useful than idle. If I help her, perhaps people will notice me for something grander than a good shawl. I'm working toward finding out where those shadows went.

OPTIONS:
- Talk to Pip Pumbleton about her brother's missing shadow and what she has seen (for: learning what is really happening to the children, and showing I care)
- Ask Mags Ragwort what she has heard about the peddler and whether she buys or sells any bits of finery (for: gossip, and maybe a bit of lovely trim for myself)
- Go to Fizzlewick's sweet shop and see what Nell can make for five buttons (for: a small treat or trinket, and a warm place to think)
* Go over to Pip and ask her plainly what she knows about Mister Tibbersnatch and her brother's shadow (for: finding out how to help the sleeping children, and being the sort of person who notices)
DO: I sweep over to Pip with my shawl pulled tight and say, "Goodness, Pip, you look as worn as an old dishcloth, and still on your feet! Tell me everything about your brother's shadow, and about that peddler's wagon. What did you see? I've got a thimble and a pair of quick hands, and I'd like to help."
JOURNAL: Pip is the only one here who's actually doing something about the sleeping children, and I'd rather be useful than fret in the dark. Maybe if I help, people will see I'm more than a girl who hems other folks' hats. I'm working toward finding out what the toys do and getting those shadows back.

OPTIONS:
- Talk to Pip Pumbleton about her missing-shadow plan and ask what she's seen (for: learning what is really happening to the children, and not facing the night alone)
- Walk over to Fizzlewick's and ask Nell what she's heard about the peddler's toys (for: gossip and a clue, and somewhere warm and bright to be)
- Show Mags Ragwort my silver thimble and ask what odds and ends she'd trade for ribbon or feathers (for: getting something fine of my own)
* Go to Pip and ask her what she means to do about the shadows, and offer to come along (for: finding out the truth, and being someone worth noticing in a brave moment)
DO: I sweep over to Pip, tugging my good shawl straight. "Goodness, Pip, you're the only one in this town still awake besides me! Tell me what you're planning about your brother's shadow. I've got a quick needle and a quicker pair of feet, and I'd like to come along, if you'll have me."
JOURNAL: Sleeplessness has put me in the square with the one person who's actually doing something, and that's more interesting than ribbon tonight. I want to help find out what Tibbersnatch's toys do, and if I'm brave about it, perhaps people will finally look at me twice.

OPTIONS:
- Talk to Pip Pumbleton about her brother's missing shadow and ask what she's seen (for: learning what's really going on with the shadows, and a chance to fix it)
- Go down Crooked Lane toward Gloomer's Meadow to look at Tibbersnatch's wagon (for: finding the source of the toys and the sleeping)
- Ask Mags Ragwort what she'd pay for odds and ends or if she's seen any of the toys (for: a bargain, maybe a clue, and a few more buttons)
- Head to Fizzlewick's to ask Nell what a tonic to wake sleepers would cost (for: a possible quick fix I could take credit for)
* Talk to Pip Pumbleton about her brother's missing shadow and ask what she's seen (for: learning what's really going on with the shadows, and a chance to fix it)
DO: I swing my pole off my shoulder and hop over to Pip. "Pip, chum! Heard you won't sleep till you've got your brother's shadow back. Easy as winking, I'll help you fix it, but first tell me everything. When did you last see his shadow, and did he wind one of those toys under a lamp or somewhere dark?"
JOURNAL: Pip is the one person who's wide awake and set on the same trouble I itch to fix, so she's the best place to start. If I learn how the shadows went, I can work out how to get them back, and everyone will know who did it.

OPTIONS:
- Ask Pip Pumbleton about her little brother's shadow and what she's seen of the peddler's toys (for: learning what's really going on, and getting in on fixing it)
- Walk south down Crooked Lane toward the meadow to look at Tibbersnatch's wagon (for: finding the cause of the sleeping with my own eyes)
- Pop into Fizzlewick's and ask Nell what a waking tonic would cost (for: seeing if a bargain cure can be made to order)
- Show Mags Ragwort my pockets and see what odds and ends she'd buy (for: turning my bargains into a few more buttons)
* Ask Pip Pumbleton about her little brother's shadow and what she's seen of the peddler's toys (for: learning what's really going on, and getting in on fixing it)
DO: I spin my pole off my shoulder and grin at Pip. "Pip, chum! Heard you won't go to sleep till you've got your brother's shadow back. Easy as winking, I'd say, but tell me first: when did it go, and did he wind one of those toys? And what's it cost you to stay up all night, eh?"
JOURNAL: Pip's the one person who's already set on fixing this, and I'd rather know what she's seen before I go charging off. If we fix it together, I'll make sure the town knows who did it.

OPTIONS:
- Talk to Pip Pumbleton about her little brother's missing shadow and what she's seen (for: finding out what's really going on, and a chance to be the one who fixes it)
- Go down Crooked Lane toward the drain and the fog to see what the grown-ups won't talk about (for: finding a clue about the shadows)
- Go to Fizzlewick's and ask Nell what a tonic against sleep would cost (for: a possible way to wake the children, if I can afford it)
- Show Mags my lamplighter's odds and ends and see what she'd give for them (for: a few more buttons for whatever comes next)
* Talk to Pip Pumbleton about her little brother's missing shadow and what she's seen (for: finding out what's really going on, and a chance to be the one who fixes it)
DO: I swing my pole down off my shoulder and hop over to Pip. "Pip, chum! Heard you won't sleep till you've got your brother's shadow back. Easy as winking, I'll help. What've you seen? Where did the toy come from, and did anybody see where the shadows went? And what'll it cost me to hear it all? Nothing, I hope!"
JOURNAL: Pip is the only one awake who cares as much as I do, and she's right here, so I'd rather learn what she knows before I spend my four buttons or walk into the fog blind. If I can find where the shadows went, I'll be the one who fixed it, and everyone will know it.

OPTIONS:
- Go south to Gloomer's Meadow and look closely at the peddler's wagon and his toys (for: finding out how the sleeping is done, since what can be done can be undone)
- Look into the drain halfway down Crooked Lane that grown-ups avoid (for: satisfying my curiosity about a mystery that may be connected to the shadows)
- Go north to Fizzlewick's sweet shop and ask Nell what she's noticed, maybe order a powder with my buttons (for: gathering information and parts for an anti-drowse compound)
* Go south toward the meadow, stopping at the drain on the way to peer into it and listen (for: checking the nearest mystery first, cheaply, before facing the peddler)
DO: I tuck my notebook tighter and march down the lane, goggles pulled down. "Hypothesis: the drain is rude. Test: be ruder!" I crouch at the drain's mouth, lamp-side, and peer in and listen, scribbling notes on any sound, smell or glint. I'll look for anything about the missing shadows before going on to the wagon.
JOURNAL: The drain is right here on the way, it costs nothing, and nobody else will look, so I'll start there before I meet the peddler with only four buttons and no plan. I'm working toward learning how the toys steal the children's sleep and shadows, so I can undo it.

Test: look in it, my dear colleague, and keep a polite distance until we know what it is!" I crouch at the grating, listen, and peer in with a lit match, jotting down whatever I see or hear.
JOURNAL: The drain is closest and I've always meant to look, and grown-ups avoiding it smells like a clue about the shadows. The wagon can wait a few minutes, and I'd rather know what's under the lane before I walk into the peddler's meadow. I'm working toward learning how the sleeping is done so I can undo it.

DO: Right then, my dear colleague, nobody's about, so Professor Gimbal shall inspect the drain! I crouch at the grate with my goggles pulled down, notebook open, and look and listen: any draught, any hum, any glint, any trace of shadow-stuff? Hypothesis: the drain is hiding something. Test: be nosy. I'll stop short of climbing in until I know what's down there.
JOURNAL: The drain is nearest and costs nothing, and the grown-ups' silence about it smells like a clue to the shadowless children. I'll look first and then carry what I learn down to the peddler's wagon.

OPTIONS:
- Wait in the Gearloft with Hobb to make sure the poker holds and the clock stays stopped (for: keeping the clock from striking thirteen, in case the gear slips)
- Climb down the ladder and run out to the Lopsided Square to look for Pip and see whether the children are waking (for: seeing with my own eyes that the shadows are home and the children are well)
- Ask Hobb if he needs help or a second pair of hands before I leave (for: being useful, and being noticed as part of the deed)
* Climb down the ladder, through the Tock Tower and out into the square, calling for Pip as I go (for: finding Pip and telling her it's done, and watching the children wake)
DO: I give Hobb a quick nod and a flourish of my shawl. "Hold it fast, Hobb, you were splendid!" Then I pick my way down the ladder, through the silent tower and out into the Lopsided Square, calling, "Pip! Pip Pumbleton! It's stopped, the shadows are coming home!"
JOURNAL: The clock is stopped and the shadows are tumbling home, so I want to be in the square when the children wake, and tell Pip myself. Hobb has the poker in hand, and I'd like to be there for the happy ending, with someone to see that I was part of it.

OPTIONS:
- Wait in the Gearloft with Hobb a moment and ask whether the poker will hold, in case the gear slips (for: making sure the clock stays stopped)
- Climb down the ladder to the Tock Tower and out to the square to look for Pip (for: seeing whether the children are waking and telling Pip it's done)
- Go to Gloomer's Meadow to see the jammed lullaby and the peddler's wagon for myself (for: finding out what has become of the toys and the children's shadows)
* Ask Hobb if he'll come down with me, then go down the ladder and out to the square (for: seeing the children wake, with a witness to say I was there)
DO: I tug my shawl straight and say, "Hobb, will you come down with me? I do so want to see whether the children are stirring, and a hero ought to be seen by the people he's saved." Then I take hold of the ladder and start down into the silent tower, out toward the square and Pip.
JOURNAL: The clock is stopped and the shadows are heading home, so the thing I most want now is to see the children wake and tell Pip. I'd like Hobb beside me so somebody sees we were both part of it, and I'm working toward the children waking.

OPTIONS:
- Climb down the ladder and run out to the square to find Pip and see whether the children are waking (for: seeing the thing I helped with come right, and telling Pip it's done)
- Stay a moment and ask Hobb whether the poker will hold, and whether he needs a hand keeping it there (for: making sure the clock stays stopped so the shadows keep coming home)
- Go down to Gloomer's Meadow to look at the peddler's wagon and the jar of shadows (for: finding out whether the shadows are truly free and what Tibbersnatch does now)
* Ask Hobb if the poker will hold, then head down the ladder once he says it's safe (for: making sure the stopped clock stays stopped, and then going to find Pip)
DO: I tug my shawl straight and say, "Hobb, you'll keep that poker snug, won't you? Goodness, I'd hate for all that shrieking to be for nothing. If it'll hold, I'm off down the ladder to find Pip and see the children wake. Do come and look when you can; you'd be quite the hero of the square tonight!"
JOURNAL: The clock must stay stopped or the shadows' trip home is wasted, so I check on Hobb before I go. Then I want to see the children wake with my own eyes and be there beside Pip when it happens.
